title: Former Cowboys QB Makes NFL Return Pitch to Cardinals After Gardner Minshew's Injury
description:
The Arizona Cardinals are scrambling for help under center after Gardner Minshew suffered a serious arm injury against the Seattle Seahawks.
“Hey @AZCardinals I weigh 190 pounds, but gosh, can I still rip it,” former Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci said on X.
Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew II could miss the rest of the season because of an injury to the UCL in his right arm.
According to NFL insider Adam Schefter, the Arizona Cardinals have brought in veteran quarterback Josh Johnson following Gardner Minshew’s injury.
Gardner Minshew is not the only Cardinals player dealing with an injury.
text:
The Arizona Cardinals are scrambling for help under center after Gardner Minshew suffered a serious arm injury against the Seattle Seahawks. One former Cowboys QB didn’t wait long to offer his services, throwing his name into the mix with a funny social media pitch.

“Hey @AZCardinals I weigh 190 pounds, but gosh, can I still rip it,” former Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci said on X. “Attaching flag football highlights for reference.”

Ben DiNucci started his NFL career with the Dallas Cowboys after being selected in the seventh round of the 2020 NFL Draft. He appeared in three games for the Cowboys during the 2020 season, making one start. He completed 23 of 43 passes (53.5%) for 219 yards, with no touchdowns or interceptions.

He later joined other teams, including the Denver Broncos, Buffalo Bills, New Orleans Saints, and Atlanta Falcons, but was released by each of them. After his NFL career slowed down, he got an opportunity to work in sports broadcasting.

CBS Sports hired him as a college football commentator, where he covered the Air Force-Bucknell game in August 2025. Apart from calling college football games, DiNucci also worked as a studio analyst on CBS Sports HQ.

He did get a brief chance to return to the field this season. The Denver Broncos signed quarterback Ben DiNucci to their practice squad on January 18, 2026, after their starting quarterback, Bo Nix, suffered an injury that ended his playoff season.

DiNucci was a familiar face because he had already spent the 2023 season with Denver. But now, Minshew’s injury might give him the chance he has been looking for. While DiNucci’s post clearly looked like a lighthearted satire, given that 190 lbs is incredibly light for an NFL QB, a real-life return to the field isn’t totally off the table.

DiNucci has not officially retired from football, and his recent stint staying in shape on Denver’s practice squad means there is little to no rust if a team needs a backup.

Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew II could miss the rest of the season because of an injury to the UCL in his right arm. According to ESPN, he is undergoing further medical checks to find out whether he needs surgery. Doctors are expected to determine if the injury requires an operation that would end his season.

Minshew injured his arm with 0:11 seconds left in the first half against the Seattle Seahawks. Linebacker Dante Fowler Jr. hit him while he was throwing the ball, causing him to lose possession. Minshew appeared to be in pain as he left the field for halftime, but he returned and continued playing in the second half.

With Minshew likely to miss the upcoming game, rookie quarterback Carson Beck is expected to start against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The Cardinals are also planning to bring in veteran quarterback Josh Johnson from the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad as another option.

But the team is not just relying on Beck. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter, the Arizona Cardinals have brought in veteran quarterback Josh Johnson following Gardner Minshew’s injury. So bringing in another player like DiNucci might not be in the cards for the team.

Apart from that, the team is already dealing with major injury trouble. Gardner Minshew is not the only Cardinals player dealing with an injury. Head coach Mike LaFleur also confirmed that wide receiver Michael Wilson will miss the rest of the season because of a neck injury.

Center Hjalte Froholdt is also facing an injury concern and has been placed in the NFL’s concussion protocol.

Along with Minshew’s uncertain availability, these setbacks leave the Cardinals with several players unavailable ahead of their Week 10 game against the Los Angeles Rams.

text:
The New England Patriots had great health in 2025. The opposite has been true in the 2026 NFL season.

The Patriots' roster has been ravaged by injuries all year, and Sunday's Week 9 game against the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium was no exception.

Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson and starting left guard Ben Brown both exited the game early and didn't return. Starting left tackle Will Campbell also left the game, but he told reporters postgame that he's OK and would have returned if the score was closer.

Veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins did return against the Packers after missing the previous four games, but the Patriots are still without A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs at that position.

Here's a recap of notable injury updates shared by Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel at his Monday press conference.

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB

Vrabel: "No update on Rhamondre. We're wearing out the MRIs this morning, so still waiting on some of those results. And do I think that Corey (Kiner) can handle that workload? I think Corey is working extremely hard. I think Corey has done a really nice job. But there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on, just like a lot of guys, as far as recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure that we saw yesterday, for example."

Later on Monday, Adam Schefter reported that Stevenson has a knee tendon issue that does not require surgery but will likely require some missed time. Ian Rapoport clarified that it's a plantaris tendon issue and that Stevenson will miss "the next few weeks."

Ben Brown, LG

Vrabel: "He won't make it this week (vs. Lions)."

With Brown unavailable for next week's game, could the Patriots activate guard Greg Van Roten?

Vrabel: "Yeah, that's something that we'll look at. He's eligible and has been working hard to get back. So, we'll take a look at that and see where he is tomorrow or Wednesday when we practice."

A.J. Brown, WR

Does Vrabel anticipate Brown making the trip to Germany?

Vrabel: "I think that that's the plan. Certainly, there's no decision on that, but I would imagine that that's the plan. We’ll continue to work to get guys back, be healthy and help the football team. That's the goal. So, to be able to answer that right now, today, I can't do that with a few guys. But, I know that the plan is to try to get everybody that can help us to get on the plane on Wednesday, go over there and help us win."

Wide receiver DJ Moore, tight end Dalton Kincaid and wide receiver Keon Coleman all began the practice week wearing red non-contact jerseys coming out of the November 1 win over the Baltimore Ravens.
DJ Moore details Moore appears to finally be in the clear when it comes to the shoulder injury he suffered in Week 2.
Dalton Kincaid details Kincaid experienced discomfort while running a third-quarter red zone route against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18.
Keon Coleman details Coleman was a new addition to the injury report in Week 9 after appearing to make it out of the November 1 win intact.
The Bills listed Coleman as a limited participant for all three practices this week.
text:
The Buffalo Bills could be without the starting left side of their offensive line when they visit the Minnesota Vikings for Monday Night Football, but there is plenty of good news elsewhere on offense.

Set to go against the NFL's No. 2 defense, Bills' quarterback Josh Allen will have a relatively healthy arsenal at his disposal in Week 9.

Wide receiver DJ Moore, tight end Dalton Kincaid and wide receiver Keon Coleman all began the practice week wearing red non-contact jerseys coming out of the November 1 win over the Baltimore Ravens.

There were no missed practices by any of the three pass-catchers this past week, and all three have been cleared for the November 9 primetime matchup in Minnesota. They'll take on the top-ranked defense against the pass.

Buffalo, however, will be without one of its wide receivers. Josh Palmer pulled up lame while running a route in the first quarter against Baltimore. Although the severity of his hamstring injury is unknown, Palmer appears to be in jeopardy of missing multiple weeks.

Meanwhile, starting left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson are officially questionable for the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

DJ Moore details

Moore appears to finally be in the clear when it comes to the shoulder injury he suffered in Week 2.

After missing back-to-back games heading into the Week 7 bye, Moore returned to the starting lineup in Week 8 against the Ravens. Officially listed as questionable for the game, Moore proceeded to make four receptions for 82 yards and one touchdown in the 36-10 win.

Moore appears to have avoided any potential knee issue from the November 1 win. Following his final catch of the game midway through the fourth quarter, Moore was slow to get up. He went into the blue evaluation tent where he was cleared.

This week marks the first time that Moore does not carry a questionable tag heading into a game since Week 2.

Dalton Kincaid details

Kincaid experienced discomfort while running a third-quarter red zone route against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18.

He went to the locker room for evaluation, and was subsequently cleared to return. Three snaps after returning to action, Kincaid made a 14-yard fourth-quarter reception.

Still, the Bills were cautious with Kincaid coming out of the bye. He was limited all week leading up to the Ravens game, and he carried a questionable tag before playing 57 percent of snaps. The tight end made four catches for 86 yards and one touchdown.

Kincaid progressed to full strength in Week 9. He was a limited participant on Thursday before increasing to full participation on Friday and Saturday. He also ditched the red non-contact jersey.

Keon Coleman details

Coleman was a new addition to the injury report in Week 9 after appearing to make it out of the November 1 win intact. He had been dealing with an ankle issue earlier in the season, this trip to the injury report comes as a result of a shoulder problem.

The Bills listed Coleman as a limited participant for all three practices this week. The wide receiver was seen wearing a red non-contact jersey during the media-viewing portions, but he'll be available for Monday Night Football.

Leading all skill position players in offensive snaps (63), Coleman, who entered with a three-game touchdown streak, was relatively quiet against the Ravens. He made only one four-yard catch, but there was one play where he ran open deep down the middle of the field only for Allen to overthrow him on what would have been a touchdown.

title: Rams WR Puka Nacua likely to hit IR with MCL and PCL sprain, turf toe - ESPN
authors: Sarah Barshop, Michael DiRocco, Bill Barnwell, DJ Bien-Aime, Nick Wagoner, Ben Baby, Marcel Louis-Jacques, Ryan McFadden, Katherine Terrell, NFL Nation

text:
LOS ANGELES -- The Rams likely will place wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve with an MCL and PCL sprain in his right leg, as well as turf toe, coach Sean McVay said Monday.

McVay didn't give a specific timeline for how many weeks Nacua is expected to miss, but said the team believes it will be at least a month.

Nacua was hurt on the Rams' final offensive snap of Sunday's victory over the Washington Commanders. The injuries happened on third down with the Rams attempting to end the game with a conversion. Nacua rushed for 5 yards but took a hard hit on the play and briefly stayed on the ground before walking off the field.

Nacua had 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown in the victory. He was targeted 19 times by quarterback Matthew Stafford. The Rams were already without wide receiver Davante Adams, who suffered a hamstring injury in Week 6.

McVay said Monday he's "kicking himself" in retrospect about exposing Nacua to a big hit with a run play late with a 20-13 lead.

"I'd be lying to you if I said I haven't questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion and maybe ended the game that would've led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee," McVay said. "And so it's stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we've got to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine."

If Nacua does go on injured reserve, he would miss games against the Arizona Cardinals, Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers.

While McVay had previously said he didn't expect the Rams to be active before Tuesday's trade deadline, he was asked Monday whether Nacua's injury affected those plans.

"Yeah, I think you look at all avenues," McVay said. "I think you've got to look at all avenues to try to be able to solve some of the issues or situations or scenarios that have come up. And so a lot of new things that occur on a daily basis, and so I would never rule it out."

Nacua's 25 receptions over the last two games are the second most by a Rams player in the Super Bowl era, according to ESPN Research. In the two-game span, the next-closest Rams players in terms of receptions are Tutu Atwell, Colby Parkinson and Kyren Williams with four each.

Nacua missed Weeks 2 and 3 with a hip injury. In seven games this season, he has 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns.

His 70 receptions are the most through a player's first seven games of a season in NFL history, according to ESPN Research. Since Week 4, he ranks first in the NFL in receptions (65) and receiving yards.

The Rams are 5-4 but have the toughest remaining strength of schedule in the NFL, according to ESPN Analytics.

text:
Round and round the Arizona Cardinals' quarterback carousel goes.

Gardner Minshew is seeking additional medical opinions to confirm that he will need season-ending surgery on a torn UCL in his throwing arm, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported.

Minshew appeared to suffer the injury on a strip-sack by Dante Fowler in the closing moments of the second quarter during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He stayed in to finish out the game with 166 yards on 21-of-30 passing.

Should Minshew require surgery that puts him on the bench for the duration of the 2026 campaign, third-round rookie Carson Beck would be in line to start in Week 10 against the Los Angeles Rams and moving forward. Arizona also signed veteran Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad, per Schefter.

Though two undrafted rookies have logged starts this season -- the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' Jalon Daniels and Baltimore Ravens' Joe Fagnano -- Beck would become the first signal-caller from the 2026 draft class to make a start, ahead of first-rounders Fernando Mendoza (Las Vegas Raiders) and Ty Simpson (Rams).

Minshew's injury continues a period of constant change in Arizona. The Cardinals completed a trade sending Jacoby Brissett, the team's starter for the first eight games, to the Baltimore Ravens on Friday. Three days later, they could be on to QB No. 3.

Though it is a certainly an unorthodox path to giving the rookie a shot, Arizona currently sits at the bottom of the NFC West with a 3-6 record, so it's beneficial at this point to see what the club has in Beck, who threw for 11,725 yards, 88 touchdowns and 32 interceptions in a long college career that included five seasons at Georgia and a final one with Miami (Florida).

He appeared only in the Pro Football Hall of Fame game during the preseason due to injuries hampering him thereafter, but he did shine in the one outing, going 15 of 19 for 188 yards and a touchdown.

His next test will be far tougher, perhaps the most unfriendly way one could be welcomed to the NFL.

With No. 1 wide receiver Michael Wilson out for the rest of the season due to a neck injury, Beck will make his debut against the terrifying defensive line duo of Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, the latter of whom returned from injured reserve in Week 9 with a three-sack statement.

How he performs against L.A. and throughout the second half of the season could play a major factor in Arizona's future QB plans.

text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers running back Josh Jacobs needs surgery on the fractured ring finger on his right hand, and coach Matt LaFleur wouldn't rule out the possibility Monday that Jacobs would have to be placed on injured reserve.

If Jacobs is placed on IR, he would miss at least four games.

LaFleur said playing through the injury wasn't an option for Jacobs.

"I don't think he could," LaFleur said. "He tried last night. He tried to go back in, and he had no grip strength."

Jacobs twice went to the locker room during the Packers' 45-27 road victory over the New England Patriots on Sunday to see whether something could be done to protect his hand while still playing. The Packers' medical staff first tried to tape it, but then, when the staff didn't feel comfortable with that, tried a cast.

Jacobs sustained the injury in the first quarter when his hand got caught in the helmet of New England defensive back Craig Woodson. Jacobs was trying to stiff-arm Woodson near the sideline at the end of a run.

The Packers (6-3) host the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, followed by their bye in Week 11, a Week 12 game at the Los Angeles Rams on Thanksgiving Eve, a Week 13 game at the New Orleans Saints and a Week 14 game against the Buffalo Bills.

"As far as how long he'll be out, I think that's to be determined," LaFleur said.

After the game, Jacobs said he saw part of his bone sticking out, although he did not say whether it punctured the skin. He said he popped his finger back into place on his own.

"It looked nasty," Jacobs said. "[Looks] a lot better now than what it did, but we'll see. We'll see how it goes."

Jacobs already missed the first six games of the season while on the NFL's commissioner exempt list, and the league continues to investigate him for possible violations of the personal conduct policy after his May 23 arrest in an incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay and allegations by three other women of physical and verbal abuse. The Packers have continued to support Jacobs throughout the process.

In three games since coming off the commissioner exempt list, Jacobs has carried 36 times for 80 yards (a 2.2-yard average) and one touchdown. He has been more effective as a receiver out of the backfield with 11 catches for 68 yards and two touchdowns.

The Packers also played Sunday without running back MarShawn Lloyd, who sustained a knee injury in practice last week.

Without Jacobs and Lloyd, the Packers relied on Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong Jr. against the Patriots. Johnson ran for 68 yards on 14 carries, the highest single-game rushing total by a Packers running back this season. He also had the longest single rushing play for the Packers this season, a 34-yard gain in the fourth quarter. The Packers totaled 129 yards rushing, marking the first time they have rushed for more than 86 yards in a game this season. They still have the NFL's lowest-ranked rushing offense.

Nevertheless, LaFleur said the Packers might not have to add a running back because Chris Brooks could return this week. Brooks was designated to return off injured reserve last week and practiced for the first time since his Week 4 ankle injury.

The Packers also were thin at linebacker Sunday. Already without Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles) and Zaire Franklin (shin), the Packers lost Ty'Ron Hopper early in the game because of a chest injury, and Isaiah McDuffie had to come off the field for a couple of plays. LaFleur said Hopper's chest was first bothering him during pregame warmups. However, he said he does not think Hopper will miss any additional time.

The Rams have lost another star to injury.

Wide receiver Puka Nacua is likely to be placed on injured reserve after suffering a turf toe injury and spraining his MCL and PCL in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders, head coach Sean McVay said Monday.

"I'm bummed for Puka," McVay said. "I feel for him. I feel for all of our players that are getting these kinds of injuries. It's challenging, but it's an opportunity for us to adjust and adapt. The game's gonna be played, but you feel for the players first and foremost."

Nacua, a two-time Pro Bowler, has 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns in seven games this season. In the outing against Washington, he was targeted 19 times with 150 yards and a score on 14 catches.

This marks the latest in a lengthy list of ailments for Nacua this season, as he was affected by psoas soreness throughout training camp and sat Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip injury, but the turf toe and knee sprain will lead to his longest absence yet.

Nacua is set to join fellow star wideout Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR, leaving the Rams with a WR corps of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and CJ Daniels, plus a tight end group of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen that is frequently used in the passing attack.

It remains to be seen when tight end Terrance Ferguson might rejoin that group. The most athletic with perhaps the highest ceiling of Los Angeles' tight ends, he initially was expected to come off IR for Week 9 after recovering from an ankle injury, only to hurt his hamstring during Friday's practice.

Though L.A. has dealt with the absence of many big names on both sides of the ball, Nacua missing extended time will prove especially detrimental to a Rams offense that hasn't clicked at all times in 2026.

Over the past two games, Matthew Stafford has thrown for 385 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions, hardly looking like the MVP quarterback he was in 2025 and -- lacking other difference-making pass catchers -- becoming laser focused on Nacua to keep things moving.

Nacua saw a 48% target share in Week 8 against the Chargers and a 44.2% share on Sunday, meaning the Rams will have to compensate for nearly half of their recent passing offense now gone.

Should Nacua go on IR as McVay expressed is likely, he will miss the next four games (plus a bye week) against the Cardinals, Packers, Chiefs and 49ers before being eligible to return in Week 15 against the Cowboys.

text:
Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson will miss the remainder of the season due to a fracture in his neck, coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday, Nov. 9.

Wilson suffered the injury on the fourth play of Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, when the receiver was tackled by cornerback Devon Witherspoon after a 17-yard catch.

"He's such a warrior that he didn't think much of it," LaFleur said. "And then obviously when the adrenaline wore down and he got his test today, that's when we knew."

Wilson finished with a game-high 60 yards on six catches.

A third-round pick in 2023, Wilson emerged as a go-to threat for the Cardinals last year. After recording career bests of 78 catches, 1,006 receiving yards and seven touchdowns in 2025, he signed a three-year, $75 million contract extension just before the season.

In 2026, he had 51 catches for 546 receiving yards and two touchdowns.

With Arizona having traded away Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans in October, the Cardinals are left with a thin receiving corps to finish out the season. Joining Simi Fehoko are Reggie Virgil, Devin Duvernay and Harrison Wallace III. Kendrick Bourne and Jalen Brooks are currently on injured reserve.

Cardinals also lose QB Gardner Minshew II

Arizona's offense figures to look significantly different down the stretch, as quarterback Gardner Minshew II suffered a ulnar collateral ligament injury that is likely to sideline him for the rest of the season, according to ESPN.

Minshew hurt his right elbow on a strip-sack by Dante Fowler Jr. at the end of the first half. He remained in for the rest of the contest, however, and finished with 166 yards on 21-of-30 passing.

text:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- The Cardinals' offense took two major blows Monday.

Quarterback Gardner Minshew II likely needs season-ending surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament, sources told ESPN, and wide receiver Michael Wilson will miss the rest of the season with a neck injury, coach Mike LaFleur said.

Sources told ESPN that Minshew is seeking additional medical opinions to confirm whether he'll need the UCL surgery.

Minshew was injured on a hit on the last play of the first half from Seattle Seahawks linebacker Dante Fowler Jr. Fowler hit Minshew as he was throwing, forcing a fumble. Minshew appeared to be in pain on the ground and then as he walked off to the locker room at the intermission but continued to play for the rest of the game.

With Minshew expected to be out, the Cardinals are set to turn to rookie quarterback Carson Beck on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams. The team also plans to sign veteran Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

A source told ESPN that Wilson fractured a vertebra and is expected to be in a brace for the next six weeks to two months. LaFleur said he's not worried about Wilson's injury being long-term.

The injury happened on the Cardinals' fourth offensive play when Wilson hauled in a 17-yard pass from Minshew and was then tackled by Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon. Wilson landed on his head but only told the Cardinals that he had a kink in his neck.

"He's such a warrior that he didn't think much of it," LaFleur said. "And then obviously when the adrenaline wore down and he got his test today, that's when we knew."

Wilson finishes his season with 546 yards and two touchdowns on 51 catches. He was on pace for his second straight 1,000-yard season. Wilson signed a three-year extension in September worth $75 million, with $47 million guaranteed.

Wilson is the latest Cardinals receiver to be lost.

After trading Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans in Week 5, the Cardinals lost Jalen Brooks and Kendrick Bourne for the season with wrist and ankle injuries, respectively. Arizona is now down to Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay, Reggie Virgil and Harrison Wallace III as its only active receivers. Recently signed receivers Zay Jones, Shedrick Jackson and James Proche II are currently on the practice squad.

LaFleur said he has never experienced as many injuries at a single position as he has this season.

During a team meeting Monday, LaFleur said he told his players that there is "a lot of opportunity" after all the injuries.

"A lot of opportunity for guys to go out there and show us what they got," LaFleur said. "So, where there's setbacks, there's setups for success. So, we'll go from there."

Who will throw to the remaining receivers is also in limbo.

Beck spent last week as the second-string quarterback following the first eight weeks as the emergency third.

LaFleur said there won't be any major changes to the offense if Beck were to take it over.

"Yeah, I mean it's not like it's the difference between a wing-T offense and a spread offense," LaFleur said. "Foundationally, we're going to do a lot of the similar stuff and a lot of the stuff that Carson likes and is good at is the same stuff that Gardner likes. They like this system, and so that's not a hard one."

text:
Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said during a press conference on Monday that wide receiver Michael Wilson suffered a "fracture in his neck area" on the fourth play of Sunday's loss to the Seattle Seahawks.

Wilson played through the injury and finished the game, but will miss the remainder of the season. The wide receiver had also been playing through two broken ribs. He brought in six of his seven targets for 60 yards against the Seahawks.

Arizona was relying on Wilson to be its No. 1 wide receiver. His breakout season last year, plus a strong start this year, gave the franchise the confidence it needed to trade away Marvin Harrison Jr. earlier this season.

Without Wilson and without Harrison, Arizona's wide receiver depth is sufficiently depleted. Barring other signings, the Cardinals' top wideout options are currently Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Harrison Wallace III, and Devin Duvernay.

Wilson had played in all nine games for Arizona this season. He finished the year with 546 yards and two touchdowns.

He has been the team's most productive wideout in receptions, yardage and touchdowns, trailing only star tight end Trey McBride in all three categories.

Arizona has a rough schedule over the next two weeks. The Cardinals play the Los Angeles Rams and the Kansas City Chiefs. Arizona then faces the Washington Commanders and the Philadelphia Eagles before its Week 14 bye.

Wilson isn't the only injury that the Cardinals have to deal with this week. Quarterback Gardner Minshew took a shot to his throwing arm in the loss to Seattle. He favored it but stayed in the game. LaFleur said they were reviewing imaging of Minshew's elbow and arm to see what he might be dealing with.

text:
Former Oklahoma defensive tackle and NFL rookie Gracen Halton saw his season come to an end on Sunday.

Halton, who the San Francisco 49ers selected in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, suffered a broken ankle in his team’s 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Halton was one of the NFL’s best defensive rookies before suffering his injury. The rookie defensive lineman notched 15 total tackles, nine solo tackles, five tackles for loss, two sacks, a forced fumble and a scoop-and-score touchdown in eight games, six of which he started.

At Oklahoma, Halton helped the Sooners’ defense improve in each of his four years with the program.

Halton registered 84 tackles, 17.5 tackles for loss, 8.5 sacks, three forced fumbles, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries and a scoop-and-score touchdown across 47 games.

The rising star defender will look to get healthy by the start of the 2027 season. San Francisco currently sits atop the NFC standings at 7-1.

Former OU edge rusher seals game for Broncos

Ex-Oklahoma edge rusher Nik Bonitto helped the Denver Broncos ice their 26-21 win over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

With 1:24 left in the game, Bonitto hit Panthers quarterback Bryce Young, forcing him to fumble. Players battled for the ball for a few seconds before Bonitto was there to scoop it up and give Denver possession.

The Broncos ran the ball three times and got a first down to seal their six-point win. In addition to Bonitto’s strip sack, he logged one other tackle for loss.

Bonitto is playing his fifth season with the Broncos. Across his first four years, he notched 138 tackles, 44 tackles for loss and 37 sacks and was selected to the Pro Bowl twice.

Before becoming one of the league’s best pass rushers, Bonitto was a star in Norman. He spent four years at OU from 2018 to 2021 and earned All-American honors twice.

Baker vs. Caleb

Two former Oklahoma quarterbacks — Baker Mayfield and Caleb Williams — squared off in primetime on Sunday, when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers battled the Chicago Bears.

In what was a back-and-forth game, Williams led a game-winning drive to help the Bears escape with a 27-24 victory.

Both quarterbacks struggled with ball control. Williams threw four interceptions, while Mayfield threw two. But the two of them each had plenty of notable moments.

Mayfield helped the Bucs rally back after falling into a 14-0 hole. He didn’t score any touchdowns but regularly led Tampa Bay’s offense down the field in the second half, and Mayfield also ran into the end zone for the game-tying two-point conversion with 2:51 left.

Williams finished the game with 279 yards and two touchdowns in addition to his four picks. On the final drive, Williams found tight end Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up the game-winning field goal.

With the win, Chicago improved to 7-2, while Tampa Bay dropped to 3-6.

text:
Over the weekend, reporting emerged that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he intends to return to play in 2026.

Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter, however, was not inclined to give any update on the star QB in his Monday press conference.

Jackson is reportedly out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb. He is currently on injured reserve.

Minter was asked what the chance is that Jackson will be able to return this season.

“You know, I’m going to keep most of the conversations between Lamar and I between Lamar and I,” Minter said. “Again, just like before, it’s a guy when you’re dealing with something, that no one wants to be on the field more. He’s probably going to do everything he can to put himself in position [to play]. But I’ll leave it at that.”

Minter also did not say whether or not Jackson requires or already has had surgery.

“I’m going to keep all that stuff between me and him,” Minter said.

Does that mean the public won’t know the nature of Jackson’s injury and if he can return?

“You may know, but that’ll come from him,” Minter said.

There was one more follow-up in the press conference, with Minter being asked if it’s accurate to say Jackson’s thumb was fractured and dislocated.

Minter chuckled before saying, “Again, that is specifics. I’ll keep it between me and him.”

Jackson has technically started five games this season. But he played just a half against Tennessee and threw only one pass against Buffalo before having to exit due to injury.

Jacoby Brissett is now set to take over as Baltimore’s starting quarterback with Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve.

text:
Patrick Mahomes has powered the Kansas City Chiefs through an impressive career trajectory, highlighted by multiple Super Bowl titles and over 35,000 passing yards. During their recent Week 9 matchup against the New York Jets, the star signal-caller delivered a steady 242-yard, two-touchdown effort to help secure a 35-12 victory and lift the team's record to 6-2.

When elite franchise leaders undergo sudden medical evaluations after taking heavy hits, the immediate results can dictate the entire outlook of a competitive season.

QB Patrick Mahomes receives positive test results after recent hit

Mahomes took a hit to his elbow during the win over the Jets. He left the game briefly but returned to finish. The team scheduled an MRI as a precaution.

"QB Patrick Mahomes underwent an MRI following today's win and sources say the tests did not reveal a major injury. Mahomes' elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swelling. But so far, so good. Mahomes did go back in the game." Ian Rapoport reported.

Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes without an interception after returning to the field against the Jets, proving his passing mechanics remained stable under pressure despite the physical contact.

The clean imaging results provide a massive sigh of relief for the Chiefs' medical staff as they design a treatment and recovery plan for the franchise quarterback ahead of Week 10.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid noted that while the medical staff will exercise normal caution during practices, the quarterback's competitive drive and quick recovery from minor setbacks have consistently kept him at the forefront of the team's weekly game plans.

Mahomes' ability to shake off the initial contact and finish the matchup underscores the physical resilience he has consistently displayed throughout his career in Kansas City. Mahomes is expected to remain active as the season continues.

With Mahomes cleared of structural damage, the Chiefs can resume standard preparations for their upcoming matchup, knowing their offensive leader remains firmly at the center of their championship pursuit.

text:
In the second quarter of the Kansas City Chiefs’ 35-12 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday, the home crowd underwent a major injury scare as quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a heavy hit from rookie pass rusher David Bailey and was immediately in obvious pain from his right elbow.

Mahomes fumbled on the play, and the Jets took over. He was instantly seen working with trainers on the sideline and throwing the ball. When the Chiefs got the ball back to close the first half a few plays later, the face of the league still had his helmet on and retook the field. Mahomes would finish the game until backup Justin Fields came on for Kansas City’s final offensive series with most of the team’s reserves.

Speaking after the game, Mahomes confirmed he still does not know exactly what the diagnosis will ultimately be.

“I haven’t gotten that,” said Mahomes. “We’re going to do some testing whenever I get done with this media stuff, and we’ll get a better understanding of it. I’m sure [head coach Andy] Reid will give you an update tomorrow.”

The quarterback reported feeling good after the game, but he suspects there will be some pain the next day and will immediately begin managing the injury.

“I feel good now,” continued Mahomes. “Obviously, you get the win and the adrenaline’s pumping. I’m sure I’ll be sore tomorrow, but we’ll get right to it. We’ll get to work on it, and we’ll get ourselves ready to go. It’s great to get the win now, now it’s about getting ourselves ready for next week.”

Later on Sunday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that a post-game MRI revealed Mahomes did not suffer a “major injury.”

At the time of the injury, neither Reid nor Mahomes knew immediately whether he would return. Reid’s attention went exclusively to getting Fields ready to enter the game if needed.

“You’ve got to get Justin ready quickly,” the coach explained. “That’s kind of where you’re at on the field. You let your medical people take care of that. Then you put everything back there and get the other guy going. He’s a tough kid. If there’s any way he can come back from something, he’s coming back. I didn’t know until we were getting ready to start that series.”

Mahomes also had lingering memories of a home game last December when he suffered a torn ACL.

“You just never know,” he remarked. “Obviously, I had the knee injury last year. You never know what’s going to be the final result or outcome of an injury. At the same time, you just try to let the doctors and trainers do their work. It’s something that scares you more than anything, but we were able to get out there and give it a go.”

Although he reiterated there is still a process to come, Mahomes’ confidence increased when he realized he could still throw, hopefully ruling out major elbow ligament damage.

“Once I could throw the football,” he recalled, “from the stories you hear whenever you can grab the ball and try to throw it, you can’t throw. Once I throw the football, I knew hopefully it wasn’t ligament type stuff. It was more muscle type stuff. That will be important to get worked out this week.”

The injury clearly impacted Mahomes on the Chiefs’ next few offensive series. However, the superstar saw marked improvement as the game went on.

“I felt like out of the half, I wasn’t throwing the ball the way I wanted to,” Mahomes observed. “As the game went on — and we continued to work through it and it kind of got warmed back up — I thought I started throwing the ball better towards the end of the second half. That will be important this week is kind of getting the swelling and the fluid out of it so I can be ready to go from the first snap next week.”

A major injury from 2025 ending his season may have made observers forget the toughness Mahomes has shown throughout his career. Sunday should serve as a strong reminder.

“If I’m able to play, I’m going to play,” Mahomes declared. “That’s part of the game. That’s part of playing. It scares you in moments when you get some pain in certain areas of your body. It obviously didn’t feel great, but I was able to get it worked on a little bit — especially at halftime — and then was able to go out there and play the rest of the game.”

Reid expects Mahomes to continue being the strong example to the rest of the team as he has through prior injuries.

“When you have a quarterback that is tough, it affects everybody,” the coach stressed. “That’s that position. They’re supposed to take everybody’s game and help raise it. Part of that is that sometimes when you’re banged up a little bit — you’re in a vulnerable position back there so you’re going to get banged up a little bit — that you’re able to get back up and go. Nobody does it better than he does it.”

The Chiefs did report two other injuries during Sunday’s game. Tackle Jaylon Moore left the game with an ankle injury and was ruled doubtful to return. Wide receiver Xavier Worthy was immediately ruled out in the fourth quarter with a hamstring injury.

“As far as the injuries go,” Reid stated, “Xavier tweaked his hamstring. I don’t know exactly how bad that is right now. Then, Jaylon Moore hurt his ankle. We’ll see how he works out here in the next day or so.”

The Chiefs’ receiving corps has already suffered heavy injury throughout the year. Mahomes expects the backups to step up in Worthy’s expected absence.

“[Worthy] was having a good day today,” lamented Mahoems. “He made some tough, physical catches especially down there at the goal line. Hopefully, it’s not as bad as it looked out there. I haven’t gotten to talk to him or the trainers or anything like that. It’s kind of that next man up mentality. We’ve had guys that have gotten reps because of the injuries. They’ll have to step in and make the plays happen whenever their number is called.”

Some positive injury news could be coming for Kansas City. CBS sideline voice Tracy Wolfson reported before the game that the Chiefs were confident that cornerback Mansoor Delane and defensive tackle Peter Woods — their pair of first-round rookies — would return in Week 10. Delane has missed the last two games with a shoulder injury. Woods left Kansas City’s Week 8 game against the Denver Broncos with a neck injury and did not play Sunday.

text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Monday that quarterback Patrick Mahomes is considered day-to-day with his right elbow injury, an injury he sustained in Sunday's win over the New York Jets. Reid shared that Mahomes was in the Chiefs' training facility Monday morning to receive treatment for his injury.

Following the game, an MRI scan didn't reveal any major injury to Mahomes' elbow, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

"It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick," Reid said Monday. "It looks like it's just a matter of [getting] some rehabbing in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. We'll just see where it goes from there. He's in good spirits."

Late in the second quarter, Jets edge rusher David Bailey hit Mahomes' right arm while he was attempting a pass, as edge rusher Will McDonald IV and defensive lineman Darrell Jackson Jr. also hit the star quarterback on the play. Although Mahomes grimaced after he hit the turf, he was able to flex his elbow on the sideline, threw a couple of warmup passes and returned to the game without missing an offensive snap.

"If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes said after the game. "That's part of the game. It scares you in moments, when you get some pains in certain areas of your body. Obviously, it didn't feel great, but I was able to kind of get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime."

Mahomes finished Sunday's game completing 23 of his 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns, even though he averaged just 2.8 air yards per attempt, his second fewest in a game in his career, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. The Chiefs' next game is Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta.

Throughout this week, the Chiefs' training staff is expected to monitor Mahomes in hopes of reducing the swelling in his elbow and his pain when throwing the ball. Reid said he didn't know if Mahomes would be able to have his full reps during the Chiefs' three practices this week.

"We'll see where he's at [Wednesday]," Reid said. "He feels pretty good today. He's sore, but I'm glad we're not practicing today."

Malik Willis, MIA (groin)

Mahomes: At the time of Mahomes' injury in Week 9, it looked as though we were watching a QB who may be done for the season. But after exiting due to an elbow injury, Mahomes was able to return in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Mahomes completed 23-of-31 passes for 242 yards and two scores, posting fewer than 20 fantasy points for the fifth time in the past six games.

Kenneth Walker III continues to be the focal point of the offense as the passing game lacks depth and a vertical threat. The Chiefs face the Falcons in Week 10 and Mahomes is considered "day to day" at this point. Should he sit, Justin Fields would draw the start, a downgrade for receivers like Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce. Walker would be relied on more heavily but could suffer with defenses keying in on the run game.

Seahawks QBs: Head coach Mike Macdonald already went on the radio Monday and said Darnold will be out Week 10 against the Raiders. Lock underwent tests on an oblique injury he suffered Sunday and those came back "good," so he's in line to start again. The Raiders have been a great fantasy matchup for QBs this season, allowing the fifth-most points to the position. However, the Seattle offense has struggled a bit with lack of depth behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Lock is back in the QB2 streaming convo for Sunday and isn't a bad spot start if you have Caleb Williams or Bo Nix on bye.

McCarthy: New York was able to sneak out of Philly on Sunday with a win. But McCarthy was forced to exit for a period of time to a hip injury. Head coach John Harbaugh has already told reporters McCarthy looks "like he's going to play" in Week 10 against Washington on TNF. The quick turnaround isn't ideal and we could see Jameis Winston back as the starter if McCarthy can't play.

The offense didn't look great against the Eagles, though they weren't much of a threat as the Giants' defense put the clamps on Joe Milton. We've seen both McCarthy and Winston elevate the passing game, so there isn't much change there in terms of how we approach Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely. Cam Skattebo should also be back to help the run game in Week 10 after missing Sunday's game. You were likely only starting McCarthy in deep superflex formats anyway.

Running Back

Rhamondre Stevenson, NE (knee)

TreVeyon Henderson, NE (illness)

Cam Skattebo, NYG (hamstring) — In line to return

Josh Jacobs, GB (finger) — Out a max of three weeks

Patriots RBs: Stevenson exited Sunday's blowout loss to the Packers early and did not return. Henderson has missed the past two games after being hospitalized due to "unexplained neurological symptoms." Stevenson is set to undergo an MRI on Monday and we'll see what the deal is. If Stevenson and Henderson are sidelined in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany, Corey Kiner would take over as the lead back. He finished with a solid 8-55-1 rushing line against Green Bay, though most of that production was on a fourth-quarter drive when the game was essentially over. Lan Larison would be the RB2 for New England, but the Pats could explore adding a back.

Jacobs: On the other side of that game, Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the win over the Patriots and didn't return. Rushing duties were then split between Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson with MarShawn Lloyd out. Johnson rushed for 68 yards on 14 carries with a score. He looked pretty good running the ball for a team that has struggled to do so all season. But it was also in a blowout. Even so, Johnson is a proactive add off the waiver wire with Jacobs expected to be out until at least Week 13. Green Bay faces the Vikings in Week 10 before the bye and it would be hard to trust any Packers RB against one of the best defenses in the NFL. Johnson will be a risky flex play against Minnesota in Week 10. Strong isn't a bad add in deeper PPR formats while keep an eye on Lloyd, who could be back soon.

Wide Receiver

Puka Nacua, LAR (knee)

Luther Burden III, CHI (concussion) — on bye

Ladd McConkey, LAC (back)

Jaylen Waddle, DEN (concussion) — on bye

Xavier Worthy, KC (hamstring)

George Pickens, DAL (hamstring)

Mike Evans, SF (Achilles)

DeVonta Smith, PHI (hamstring)

A.J. Brown, NE (knee)

Carnell Tate, TEN (shoulder)

Deebo Samuel Sr., SF (hamstring)

Garrett Wilson, NYJ (concussion)

Nacua: The Rams sent Nacua for an MRI and we'll see what those results reveal. It's not believed that the top wideout suffered a season-ending knee injury at this point. But Nacua could end up missing games. The Rams are already without Davante Adams and there isn't much depth behind those two. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and the trio of tight ends — Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen — would need to step up. LA could also lean more on its run game with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum.

If Nacua is out, it's a downgrade to the passing game and Matthew Stafford's fantasy outlook. It's a slight bump up for Williams and Corum, both of whom are involved in the passing game plenty. The Rams take on the Cardinals before their bye in Week 11, so chances are Nacua will at least be held out in Week 10. That'll give him ample time to rest the knee before Week 12 against the Packers.

Pickens: The Cowboys held Pickens out of their win over the Colts in Week 9. As a result, CeeDee Lamb went off for 10-195-1 while third-string WR Ryan Flournoy was quiet with two catches for 53 yards. Dallas leaned on the run game, leading most of the first half. It's clear the offense missed Pickens and will need him ready for a key NFC matchup with the Niners in Week 10. If Pickens is out again, Flournoy remains an a flex option while Lamb would remain a target hog and elite WR1.

Tight End

Jake Ferguson, DAL (knee)

The Chicago Bears barely beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9 after Caleb Williams threw four interceptions and Luther Burden III fumbled the ball inside the Bears' territory late in the game, giving Tampa Bay a chance to tie the game.

On that Burden fumble, he was hit very hard in the head, leading to the Bears' WR going to the medical tent for testing. Unfortunately, the news the Bears got after the game was what was feared for the breakout WR.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, Burden has a concussion, which will put his status going forward in doubt after his scary helmet-to-helmet hit during Sunday Night Football.

Luther Burden III suffers concussion during SNF for Bears

"Bears WR Luther Burden III suffered a concussion late in Sunday night's win over Tampa Bay, now in concussion protocol," Schefter reports.

This is an unfortunate update for the Bears, especially as the wide receiver was finally breaking out in a big way this season.

Burden showed potential in 2025, and through the first half of 2026, he's nearly surpassed all of his 2025 stats from the entire season.

In nine games, Burden has 49 receptions on 65 targets (both career highs) with 644 yards and four touchdowns. He already has double the TDs he had in his rookie season and is just eight yards shy of tying his yardage total from last season.

MORE: Caleb Williams, Baker Mayfield turn 'SNF' into turnover fest as Bears overcome interceptions

But now, Burden is landing in concussion protocol after a scary hit during Sunday Night Football. Chicago could be without Burden for some time, depending on how quickly he can get through concussion protocol.

Fortunately for the Bears and Burden, he might not actually miss any time, as the Bears have a bye week in Week 10. That will give Burden two weeks to try to clear concussion protocol.

There's a real chance he doesn't miss any time due to this concussion. But clearing protocol can be tricky, and the breakout receiver isn't guaranteed to be good to go for Week 11 when the Bears come out of the bye.

This is an injury situation worth keeping an eye on, as Burden clearing protocol will be one of the biggest storylines of the Bears' bye week and their Week 11 matchup.

text:
As of Wednesday, Lions linebacker Jack Campbell had “full movement” in his lower body but not yet in his upper body after suffering a scary neck injury on Nov. 1.

Yet he can’t keep his mind off of returning to the field.

Lions head coach Dan Campbell told CBS that Jack told him, “Just make sure the house is taken care of until I can get back.”

“Are you surprised at anything for Jack? That’s Jack,” Dan Campbell elaborated to reporters after the team’s road win over the Dolphins on Sunday. “Jack is all about the goal in front of me, and ‘I’m going to attack that goal, and I’m going to destroy that goal, and I’ll move onto the next thing.’

“As you know, the way he’s wired, he will do any and everything it will take to overcome any perception of adversity. That’s the way he is.”

Jack Campbell, 26, was stretchered off and taken to a hospital after tackling Vikings tight end TJ Hockenson. The first-team All-Pro said Wednesday he was “continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body” and that he was “incredibly encouraged” by his progress.

“Every day he heals a little bit more,” Dan said of Jack on Sunday.

His teammates wore his No. 46 jersey as they arrived to the stadium for Sunday’s game, and his locker was set up with his jersey.

“It’s all we could do because I mentioned this before, he’ll take the prayers, but he didn’t want the pity,” Dan Campbell said. “He didn’t want you wasting the time thinking about him. He certainly doesn’t want us to go and not play our best ball and lose a game. So that’s what we could do, and we wanted to honor him.

“There’s nothing easy about it. This is hard because you do want to talk about it and acknowledge it, because if you just brush it under the rug that’s not fair. I mean, the guy means too much to us, and so the guys did that.”

text:
Giants head coach John Harbaugh confirmed Monday that quarterback J.J. McCarthy suffered a hip pointer in Sunday's win over the Eagles.

Harbaugh said McCarthy is "doing well" and that while it is too early to confirm, it looks like he will be able to play Thursday night against the Commanders.

Chicago Bears wideout Luther Burden is in concussion protocol following a hit to the head late during the team's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9.

The hit came late in the fourth quarter, as Burden was trying to take a screen pass up the field for a first down. He fumbled on the play, turning the ball over.

With the wideout in concussion protocol, his status for the Bears' next game is uncertain. Burden, however, will be helped by the Bears being on a bye in Week 10, giving him an additional week to recover from the injury before Chicago takes the field again.

Myles Garrett is back for the Los Angeles Rams and doing Myles Garrett things. In his first game back from injury, he recorded three sacks and a forced turnover in a 20-13 victory over the Washington Commanders.

The All-Pro pass rusher and two-time Defensive Player of the Year played just one game in his debut season with the Rams before landing on injured reserve. He was ineffective with no tackles in a Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, and it turned out that he was playing hurt.

Garrett required arthroscopic surgery to address swelling and irritation in his left knee that had lingered through training camp. From the looks of things, the surgery and time off did him some good.

When Garrett returned to the field on Sunday to face the Commanders, it took him less than one half a play to create his first turnover with his new team.

Read more about Garrett's return to the Rams in Week 9.

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes left Sunday's game against the New York Jets with an injury scare after a hit to his throwing elbow but was able to return to help lead a 35-12 win.

The hit took place in the second quarter on a sack that forced a fumble. Mahomes' right elbow bent awkwardly on the sack, and he fumbled the ball. He was in clear pain after the hit and walked to the sideline holding his right arm. The Jets took over possession after recovering the fumble.

But Mahomes was able to throw on the sideline and returned to the field before the end of the half after the Chiefs retook possession of the ball.

Mahomes didn't appear to be impacted by the injury scare and finished the day completing 230of-31 passes for 278 yards (7.8 yards per attempt) with 2 touchdowns and no turnovers.

"If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes said after the game. "In scares you in moments when you get pains in certains areas of your body, so obviously I didn't feel great. I was able to get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime, and was able to go out there and play the rest of the game."

Mahomes said he felt good after the game. "I'm sure I'll be sore tomorrow, but we'll get right to it and work on it."

Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is dealing with a hamstring injury that held him out of Week 9, and now his backup, Drew Lock is even more banged up than he entered the week.

Per head coach Mike McDonald, Lock suffered an oblique injury while starting in Darnold's place in Week 9 — on top of the severe case of tendonitis he's already been dealing with in his throwing elbow.

We'll have to monitor the statuses of both Darnold and Lock closely ahead of Week 10, when Seattle travels to face the Las Vegas Raiders ahead of the bye in Week 11.

If neither quarterback would be able to go, it would be third-stringer Jalen Milroe.

Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua went down with a knee injury late in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders on Sunday.

Nacua is set to undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of the injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, though the team does not believe that he suffered a torn ACL.

Further specifics, including how long he may be sidelined, are not yet known.

Nacua caught a short pass with about 90 seconds left at Northwest Stadium, but was brought down well short of the line to gain. It didn't appear that anything went wrong in the moment, and Nacua jumped back up and left the field normally after being tackled.

Nacua had 150 yards and a touchdown on 14 catches in the win on Sunday. It marked his third outing this season with at least 125 receiving yards, and he's now scored a touchdown in four of his past five games.

text:
The Chicago Bears managed to secure a 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9, all thanks to Cairo Santos for a clutch field goal. But in the fourth quarter, with less than four minutes left on the clock, wide receiver Luther Burden gave the Bears fans an injury scare and exited the game, leaving them arguing about a potentially missed penalty.

On a third-and-seven at the Bears' 15-yard line, quarterback Caleb Williams threw a short left to Burden for four yards. However, rookie Bucs outside linebacker Rueben Bain Jr. collided with the WR, forcing him to fumble and go down. Safety Ifeatu Melifonwu recovered the loose ball.

Burden walked off the field and entered the blue tent and didn't return to the game. Later on, head coach Ben Johnson revealed that the Bears wide receiver suffered a concussion.

Eagle-eyed fans quickly noticed that Bain and Burden's helmets collided during the play. They began accusing the referees of missing the penalty call. A helmet hit is a serious penalty and can warrant a disqualification at times. Per the rules, the offense is allowed to advance 15 yards and gets an automatic first down.

When questionable calls shape the outcome of primetime games, the integrity of the sport hangs in the balance. Stay informed on the controversies reshaping the NFL with our newsletter.

However, in Burden's case, the game continued as normal. The Bucs scored a touchdown in the ensuing drive.

Fans have noted the lack of the penalty for the troubling incident.

"I turned to my family and said exactly this immediately when it happened. Good looking out. Hope Luther is alright, he's one of our favorite players," one fan wrote in the comments.

"It's not a missed call when they see it and choose not to call it bc they need bucs to cover," one fan wrote.

"It's not missed when you just don't want to call it," another fan added.

"Yup just like MNF last week vs the Seahawks. No Bears were fined for their dirty hits," added another.

"How was this s*** not called," questioned another fan.

"Bears don't get calls at home. NFL hates the Bears," another message read.

Of course, everyone hoped for Burden's safety. But there were a few fans who claimed that it wasn't really a foul. Bain looked like he was genuinely going for a tackle and led with his shoulder. But coincidentally, he made contact with his helmet.

"Bears fan and this isnt a penalty. He didnt lead with his head, went in for a clean tackle and the contact was incidental. Hope luth is okay," one fan commented. "That's not a penalty. He was a runner and it was not the crown of the helmet," another fan wrote.

"Ducks his helmet and gets hit with shoulder, very unfortunate for burden but a good no call.

Burden left the game with seven catches for 97 yards and one touchdown. He's indeed an important weapon for Williams. But for now, the NFL community and the Bears lie in wait to see how fast Burden clears the concussion protocol.

When Patrick Mahomes injured his elbow in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the New York Jets, the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback couldn't mask his initial reaction.

Mahomes grimaced in pain after a strip-sack by David Bailey, holding his right elbow as teammates helped him off the field.

After being evaluated on the sideline, however, Mahomes went back to warming up and returned to play on the following series without missing a play.

What Patrick Mahomes said about elbow pain

"If I'm able to play, I'm gonna play," Mahomes said in a news conference after the 35-12 win. "That's part of the game. That's part of playing. It scares you in moments when you get pains in certain areas of your body.

"Obviously, I didn't feel great, but I was able to get it worked on, especially at halftime, and go out there and play the rest of the game."

On his first play back, Mahomes found tight-end Travis Kelce for a quick 12-yard connection, but kicker Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field goal as time expired.

Mahomes, who was sidelined for the remainder of last season by a torn anterior cruciate ligament suffered last December, drew a parallel to the knee injury, saying there was an initial "scary" element of uncertainty. He felt confident after throwing the ball on the sideline, however, that it not a ligament issue.

Patrick Mahomes' MRI results

Mahomes had been set to undergo additional testing, he said. An MRI on Sunday night did not reveal any major injury, ESPN's Ian Rapoport reported.

Mahomes finished with 242 yards and two touchdowns on 23-of-31 passing.

text:
SEATTLE -- Drew Lock quarterbacked the Seahawks to another victory while filling in for Sam Darnold on Sunday, and this time, he did it while playing hurt.

Already dealing with an injury to his throwing elbow, Lock suffered an oblique injury in the third quarter of Seattle's 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field. Coach Mike Macdonald said postgame that the statuses of both QBs for this coming week are uncertain, but Lock later answered in the affirmative when asked if he's confident he'll be able to play Sunday against the Raiders if his number is called.

"Drew came in and balled," said tight end AJ Barner, who scored both of Seattle's touchdowns. "That's what we expect from Drew. We've seen it before. Sam and [QB3 Jalen Milroe] did a great job, too, of just having that room all together."

Darnold was one of six Seahawks (5-4) starters who were sidelined Sunday, yet Seattle still had little trouble beating the Cardinals (3-6) for the 11th straight time, which marks the longest winning streak over any opponent in franchise history. The win got the reigning Super Bowl champions back above .500 after their 17-point loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night, which was their most lopsided defeat since December 2024.

Lock was 19-of-28 passing for 175 yards and a touchdown. While filling in for Darnold for two full games and most of a third this season, Lock has yet to turn the ball over, and Seattle has won all three times.

Macdonald called him "a beast."

"Through, not around," Macdonald said about Lock's approach, using his go-to phrase about attacking adversity. "He kind of just went after it. Our medical people deserve a shoutout too for putting a great plan together and treating Drew. Jalen Milroe too, operating our offense when he took the snaps that he took and being ready to play in case Drew couldn't go or couldn't finish. So really a great team effort.

"Really, both quarterbacks that have played, I don't know how you could get any tougher. Both guys are as tough as nails."

Lock was starting because Darnold injured a quad at the end of the Bears game, when he also played through a cracked rib he suffered on the second play.

Macdonald said postgame that he did not have a great feel for whether Darnold will be able to return this week. The Seahawks have a bye after they play the Raiders, then face the NFC West-leading San Francisco 49ers (7-1) at Levi's Stadium in Week 12.

"I think we'll probably reevaluate early in the week," Macdonald said. "I'm assuming we're probably going to have to make a decision on who we're going to get ready and how we're going to do that. Drew's situation, we'll have to evaluate that as well."

Lock took over in the season opener after Darnold suffered a glute injury on the fifth play, quarterbacking Seattle to a win over the Patriots before throwing three touchdown passes to beat Arizona the following week. He ranked sixth in QBR (82.5) during that stretch.

But in the rematch against the Cardinals, Lock didn't have the benefit of a normal week of practice. The only time he threw the ball was Thursday as Seattle tried to manage the elbow injury that had him inactive the previous two games. Lock was listed as limited in practice all three days -- as he has been on every injury report since the start of Week 6 -- and didn't throw during the early, nonpadded portion of warmups Sunday.

He tipped his cap to the organizational effort it took to get him ready to play.

"I feel like I've found my way as a guy that doesn't get reps as a backup to be ready for a game," Lock said. "So when we got to this week, it's not something that I wasn't used to, to say the least. Just mentally being as prepared as I can with tape, walk-through reps, me watching practices and being able to come out here and spin it around."

Lock hurt his oblique on a rollout throw on the second play of Seattle's opening possession of the third quarter. He was moving gingerly for the remainder of the drive -- which ended in a Jason Myers field goal -- and visited the medical tent afterward. He did not miss a snap.

Asked how he was feeling postgame, Lock said, "Not too bad" and added that he was set to get his injured oblique looked at later in the evening.

"He's a warrior," said star receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who had seven catches for 51 yards. "He played great today. He commanded the offense. I just love the flow that he gets in and gives the rest of the offense, and we certainly feel that. We know he can get the job done."

Arizona's defense entered Week 9 ranked 30th in EPA while allowing 28.3 points per game, second most in the NFL. The Cardinals managed only three official quarterback hits on Lock all game despite blitzing him on 15 of his 29 dropbacks. Seattle was playing without two offensive line starters in left tackle Charles Cross and left guard Quenton Nelson.

He did not discuss his injury with reporters after the game, and he was visibly in a good mood.
Another Commanders game ended with a head-scratching final play.

text:
Week 9 of the NFL season featured a Super Bowl favorite finally getting over .500, some magic from Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders and a bounce-back performance from an MVP candidate.

Here’s everything you need to know from Sunday.

Welcome back, Myles Garrett. So long, Puka Nacua?

Garrett, the reigning defensive player of the year whom the Los Angeles Rams traded for in the offseason, returned from a knee injury that had sidelined him for seven games and made his presence felt immediately in a 20-13 win over Washington (2-5-1). All three of his tackles ended in sacks, and his first sack also forced a fumble to help the Rams (5-4) climb above .500 for the first time.

How impactful was Garrett? In eight previous games, the Rams had 12 sacks combined.

It was the first game Garrett played alongside Aaron Donald, the superstar defensive tackle who came out of retirement to create an all-world defensive line.

The Rams might not be able to celebrate for long. On their final play of the game, star receiver Puka Nacua suffered a reported knee injury that will require more imaging Monday to determine its severity. Nacua was targeted 19 times, and he finished with 14 receptions for 150 yards and a touchdown. He did not discuss his injury with reporters after the game, and he was visibly in a good mood.

Another Commanders game ended with a head-scratching final play. With the ball on the Rams’ 31-yard line, Washington threw a short pass, then tried an unsuccessful lateral until the clock ran out. Why not try a deep pass into the end zone? Coach Dan Quinn said Washington called in two plays — one a deep ball and the other a short completion and lateral option if the Rams blitzed hard. “Didn’t love our execution at the end,” he said.

Bears survive five turnovers

The worst record in the NFC North belongs to 6-3 Green Bay. In a division that difficult, a team’s margin for error to make the playoffs is razor thin, which is why the Chicago Bears (7-2) must be one of the most relieved teams in the league after Week 9.

After having led Tampa Bay 14-0, Chicago proceeded to turn the ball over five times — four interceptions by Caleb Williams and a fumble inside its own 20-yard line by receiver Luther Burden III with 3:48 to play and Tampa Bay (3-6) trailing by eight. The Buccaneers would score a touchdown and a 2-point conversion for a tie.

Yet for all of Williams’ erratic play, his 38-yard completion in the final minute all but sealed the win by putting Chicago within range of a 38-yard field goal that Cairo Santos drilled for a walk-off 27-24 victory.

Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield added two interceptions. The six interceptions were the most combined by two quarterbacks in a game this season. Chicago is the first team to win a game while turning the ball over five-plus times since 2006.

The Chiefs end their two-game losing streak

For years, as Patrick Mahomes played, so went Kansas City. But it might be more accurate this season to say running back Kenneth Walker III is the barometer for the Chiefs’ offense.

Kansas City (6-2) ended its two-game losing streak in a 35-12 rout of the New York Jets (2-7) in which Walker bounced back with 102 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground and 41 yards with two touchdown catches through the air. He had been held to just 3.0 yards per carry in his previous two games, both Chiefs losses. Walker averaged nearly double that (5.6 yards) Sunday.

Mahomes looked like he would be leaving the game in the second quarter after his arm bent awkwardly when he was sandwiched by multiple defenders. Instead, he finished with 242 yards and two touchdowns.

Shedeur Sanders runs out of magic in overtime

Sanders led two comeback drives in the first start of his sophomore season, but he couldn’t lead the Browns all the way to a win against the New Orleans Saints.

Cleveland lost 23-22, but Sanders had some encouraging moments. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards, the second-highest passing total of his career. With the Browns trailing 16-13 in the fourth quarter, Sanders calmly led a game-tying drive for a field goal despite getting the ball with under a minute to go.

After a long drive by the Saints to start overtime, Sanders responded by leading an eight-play, 67-yard touchdown drive. But the Browns went for 2 and the win after the score, and the attempt failed, dropping Cleveland to 5-4.

The Giants keep finding a way, remain atop the NFC East

After the Giants lost quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2, New York’s season looked to be in major trouble. But head coach John Harbaugh has kept the team afloat in his first year at the helm, and the Giants improved to 5-2-1 with a win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.

New York is 4-1-1 since Dart’s injury. On Sunday, starter J.J. McCarthy had to leave the game briefly with an injury, but he returned to close out the Giants’ first win in Philly since 2013. New York is the only team in the NFC East with a winning record, even after the Dallas Cowboys beat the Indianapolis Colts.

Raiders’ regression continues; Chargers remain winless

Under coach Klint Kubiak and quarterback Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas was one of the season’s early surprises as it started 3-0. In hindsight, those three wins were against subpar competition in the Miami Dolphins, the Los Angeles Chargers and the New Orleans Saints. After Sunday’s 38-17 loss at San Francisco, the Raiders (4-5) have lost five of their last six games. Sunday’s was the sixth consecutive game in which they have allowed 30 or more points, the longest streak in team history. As the losses mount, will Las Vegas finally turn to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza?

And yet for all of that regression from the Raiders, they still are not the AFC West team that feels the worst after nine weeks. After a 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans at home, the Chargers remain the NFL’s last winless team.

They join the 2011 Indianapolis Colts as the only teams since 2000 to start a season 0-8 the year after they made the playoffs. The lone consolation for Los Angeles fans is that at least one streak ended. Justin Herbert’s fourth-quarter touchdown pass ended a run of 37 consecutive drives without scoring a touchdown. Herbert has now gone 10 consecutive starts without multiple touchdowns.
